summary: Independent review of the three-thin-bar resting volume pull. THE OPERATOR'S REASONING IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART: the purple (short) segment is LOW VOLUME BY NATURE — that is the waiting period — and the volume arrives WITH the flip, which is the exact moment the resting order exists to catch. A one-bar volume floor therefore systematically pulls the order immediately before the event it is waiting for. LIVE COST MEASURED TODAY: FTFT 14:37 vol 8,974 thin, 14:38 vol 2,301 thin, 14:39 vol 25,750 placed at stop 2.8843 limit 2.8987, 14:40 vol 5,515 cancelled by V2-RESTING-CANCEL reason=liquidity_floor on ONE thin bar, 14:41 vol 61,849 flip=BUY with the bar travelling low 2.8501 to high 2.9300. We cancelled SIXTY SECONDS before the flip, and once the segment turned long the resting entry no longer applied, which is why nothing was placed again. THE CHANGE IS EXACTLY SCOPED: the cancel threshold becomes three consecutive sub-floor completed bars; one or two thin bars keep the managed rest alive; any bar at or above the floor resets the streak to zero. The volume floor stays 10,000 and the reprice fraction stays 0.5 percent, both confirmed live in pid 646497 and neither touched. I CHECKED A SUSPECTED DEFECT AND IT WAS MY MISREAD: the diff appears to show an unconditional counter reset after the increment, which would make the three-bar threshold unreachable; in the actual file that reset is inside the long-state branch, a different block entirely. Reading the diff without context nearly produced a false P1 from me. MUTATIONS, ALL RED: revert the threshold to 1 bar turns FIVE controls red INCLUDING the real-tape replay; set it to 9999 so it never cancels turns 4 red, so the over-correction is pinned too; make the streak never reset on a good bar turns 1 red; move the reprice threshold turns 1 red. THE CONTROL THAT MATTERS MOST is test_ftft_20260911_real_tape_stays_resting_through_the_flip: it replays the REAL production bars (8,974 / 2,301 / 25,750 / 5,515 / 61,849) at PRODUCTION config — flip-owned on, account-neutral discovery on, reclaim off, hold-confirm off, reprice 0.5, floor 10,000 — and it FAILS when the code is reverted to one bar. Evidence from the actual failure, not a fixture. AND THE SLOT DANGER I FLAGGED HAS ITS OWN CONTROL: test_volume_pull_replaces_without_consuming_the_first_slot, because a re-place after a volume pull must not be suppressed as first_slot_already_consumed, which is the trap we spent today fixing on TNON. THE PR'S OWN WORDING IS CORRECTLY HEDGED AND MUST STAY THAT WAY: a fill was likely, not guaranteed. The control proves the order was STILL RESTING when the flip bar arrived; it cannot prove a stop-limit fill from a one-minute bar, and nobody should upgrade that claim later. SECOND DEFECT THIS ALSO ADDRESSES, found while investigating a separate operator question: the same 15:09 liquidity_floor cancel pulled BOTH the Schwab rest and the Webull mirror; when Schwab re-placed at 15:11:03 and filled at 15:11:12, the Webull leg — deliberately created only AFTER the Schwab order confirms, a measured 1.3s median lag across 42 pairs today — arrived at 15:11:13 with its stop below market and was rejected STOP_PRICE_MUST_BE_GREAT_THAN_MARKET_PRICE. Had the pair stayed resting from 15:08 there would have been no fresh placement and no race, so this change also removes most of the single-broker-fill exposure. Controlled full unit pair vs base f9dfd398: base 46 failed / 3682 passed, head 46 failed / 3686 passed, ZERO new failure names and ZERO fixed. Ruff clean. Ancestor PASS. Reviewer differs from the author. No findings; nothing withheld.
